correctness.rationale: The source-removal blocks canonically determine all cross-part arc directions. Multiple first-block vertices give multiple sources. In each of the four exceptional codes, one vertex has every incident edge forced into every out-branching, so deletion disconnects it. For every other code, the proof gives one entering arc for every non-source vertex and explicitly lists enough unused cross edges to connect the complement. All four positive cases were checked for direction validity and complement connectivity. An independent brute-force parent-choice enumeration agrees for every canonical word with \(4\le n\le7\), while the explicit constructions replay for all words with \(4\le n\le30\). The finite checks are supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The family \(K_{3,n}\), for \(n\ge4\), is the first complete-bipartite regime where a non-separating out-branching can exist at all: \(K_{2,n}\) and \(K_{3,3}\) fail the necessary two-edge-disjoint-spanning-tree edge count. The result therefore resolves the natural boundary family orientation-by-orientation, converts a general matroid-intersection decision into four transparent obstruction codes, and separates the unique-source condition from the genuinely non-separating condition. This is a structural classification motivated directly by the new 2026 problem, not an arbitrary finite slice.
